The Windows clock probe's answer with its pwsh tags (E15.S1b) - CAPTURED, not synthetic.

Source:   The Windows host's own Windows PowerShell 5.1 (unelevated, 64-bit, the System32 one) on the owner's machine,
          on 2026-10-12 at 07:58:47Z. Read-only: the probe's script (HealthCommands.ClockScript as E15.S1b builds it) was
          started from a PowerShell 7 helper exactly as the product starts it - powershell.exe -NoProfile -NonInteractive
          -Command <the script>, the argv as a list - with its stdout saved as written (UTF-8, LF).
          This machine has NO MSI PowerShell 7: C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7\pwsh.exe is absent (the Store package is
          installed, which the probe never looks at), so the capture is the ABSENT shape - the known folder and the
          environment both name C:\Program Files, pwsh.msi=absent, pwsh.signature empty. The verified shape (file, signed)
          was observed on the same day by pointing the same look at the Store package's pwsh.exe (file, signed) and is
          DERIVED in the tests from this capture, said so there (PwshEngineFixture.Verified).

Files:
  powershell-clock.out   powershell.exe -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command <ClockScript>  (Running, Automatic; absent)
  captured-at.txt        the instant of the capture (the Windows clock, UTC)
